subject: Critical Thinking
title: Moral Relativism vs. Moral Universalism: Is Anything Always Wrong?
description: A short lesson to help you apply Moral Relativism vs. Moral Universalism: Is Anything Always Wrong?.

hook.text: Some cultures practiced human sacrifice. Others practice capital punishment. Others ban both.

buildup.text: Moral Relativism vs. Moral Universalism sets up the core claim, the assumptions, and the stakes.

discovery.text: Moral Relativism vs. Moral Universalism reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Moral Relativism vs. Moral Universalism has a twist: the obvious interpretation usually breaks down.

climax.text: Moral Relativism vs. Moral Universalism matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: The goal is not certainty, but sharper thinking.

quiz.question: What is the paradox of extreme moral relativism?
options: If all moralities are equally valid, then anti-relativist moralities are also valid, creating a contradiction
